data.name: Rehaam
data.gender_notes: Rehaam is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is content and satisfied with what Allah has given to him. The name Rehaam carries the meaning “Content, Satisfied, Contented” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Rehaam usually hope their child will grow to embody content, satisfied, contented and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for one who is spiritually content and satisfied with his relationship with Allah.
data.etymology: Rehaam belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Content, Satisfied, Contented.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rehaam total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

In many Islamic traditions, the prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized the importance of being pleased with Allah's decree and the blessings bestowed upon us, as stated in various Hadith and Quranic verses. Rehaam, as a name, encourages individuals to embody this quality and strive for inner peace and happiness, rather than constantly desiring material possessions or worldly success.

This concept is known as "rida" in Islamic philosophy, which denotes the state of being pleased with Allah's decree and finding peace in submission to His will. By embracing the name Rehaam, an individual is not only reminded of the importance of inner peace and contentment, but is also encouraged to cultivate this virtue through daily practices such as regular prayer, seeking knowledge, and performing good deeds, ultimately drawing closer to Allah and finding spiritual fulfillment.
